comments.body:
**Review of the full proof and fixes applied (issue is the generic "Proof" task, so I audited the whole argument).**

The overall strategy is sound: NP-hardness of GMM-MLE via a many-one reduction from an integral-threshold variant of Euclidean k-means, glued by a likelihood/cost "sandwich" (Lemma lem:sandwich), plus tractability results for k=1 and constant (d,k). I verified the sandwich numerically (exact centroids + uniform weights sit between the two bounds, tightly), and the integrality/scaling reduction (thm:kmnp, lem:sep, cor:dich). Those are correct.

I found and fixed TWO genuine gaps, both in the positive half of the paper:

1. Corollary cor:approx (additive inapproximability) used a non-effective comparison. The proof claimed the pivot U = -T/(2σ²) - n log k is rational because n log c_σ was removed — but U still contains n log k, which is IRRATIONAL for k≥2, so comparing \tilde L to U-(3/2)n log k is not an exact rational test. FIX: introduced a rational pivot ρ = -β - (5/2) n A, where β = T/(2σ²) ∈ ℚ and A ∈ ℚ is any rational with (3/5)log k ≤ A ≤ (7/5)log k (poly-time computable). Proved ρ lands in the separation band [-β-(7/2)n log k, -β-(3/2)n log k], so the single RATIONAL comparison \tilde L ≥? ρ decides k-Means_ℤ in both YES and NO cases under additive error < (1/2)n log k. (Band arithmetic verified numerically.)

2. Proposition prop:dk (constant (d,k) ∈ P) had an unjustified "consistent assignment" step. The lifted-arrangement enumeration produces witnesses w not necessarily satisfying the lift constraint, and the text asserted without proof that such w give an acyclic labeling. Made rigorous via the SCORE-FIELD IDENTITY: with d_{i,l}(w) := q_l − ⟨x_i,μ_l⟩ one has a_{i,ll'}(w) = d_{i,l}(w) − d_{i,l'}(w) for EVERY w. Hence each point's comparisons are governed by one scalar field and form a total preorder — cyclicity is impossible — so j(i) ∈ argmin_l d_{i,l}(w) is always well defined. Tightened correctness: equal sign vectors ⇒ same argmin set ⇒ for the genuine optimal w* this equals the nearest-center set, and recentering at centroids only lowers cost, giving \widehat{OPT}=OPT(X,k) exactly. (While fixing this I caught and corrected a sign error; nearest center = argmin of the corrected d_{i,l}; verified numerically.)

Also sanity-checked the full algorithm: enumerating partitions induced by center tuples recovers exact brute-force k-means OPT on many random small instances.

LaTeX integrity verified (environments balanced, all \ref/\eqref/\cite resolve, braces balanced; no toolchain to compile).

Conclusion: with these two fixes the proof is complete and rigorous — NP-hardness (k≥2, fixed isotropic Gaussian), additive (1/2)n log k inapproximability, k=1 closed form, constant-(d,k) polynomial time, with honest caveats on APX-hardness (rem:mult). Resolving.
